set.text: Many students believe that any image found online is free to use. In fact, most pictures are protected by copyright, which means that the creator decides how they may be used. Using a photo in a private school assignment is often allowed, but posting it on a public website may require permission. Some creators share their work under licenses that let others use it if they give credit; websites for such images usually show the terms on each page. If you are not sure, choose an image you have taken yourself. Always note the creator's name, the source and the license. This habit not only protects you from legal problems, but also shows respect for the person who made the picture.

patches.why: "This habit" referred to the sentence about choosing one's own image, so Q5 (benefit of crediting) was ambiguous; moved that sentence before "Always note...". Passage text only.
